title: AEO vs GEO vs SEO: What's the Difference, and Which Do You Need?
metaTitle: AEO vs GEO vs SEO: Differences and Which You Need
metaDescription: AEO and GEO are two labels for earning a mention in AI answers; SEO is the foundation under both. See one comparison table and a test for which you need.
shortAnswer: SEO earns a ranked link and a click. AEO and GEO are two names for earning a mention inside an answer an engine shows or writes, so the real split is ranking versus being named. Google says optimizing for its AI features is "still SEO", so build on SEO first. Add AEO or GEO work only if AI answers to your buyers' questions name competitors and skip you.
intro:
Three labels make this sound like three strategies. It is closer to one foundation and two scoreboards: ranked and clicked, or named in an answer.

We build an AI visibility audit, so we have a stake here; claims link to sources and our own data is labelled. For what changes day to day on an SEO team, see [AEO vs SEO](/blog/aeo-vs-seo).

sections.heading: What do SEO, AEO and GEO each mean?
sections.body:
[SEO](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/seo-starter-guide) is making your site easy for search engines to understand and for people to find. AEO and GEO are two labels for getting named inside the answer an engine shows or writes. [Google's guide](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) lists both as terms for AI search visibility work.

- **SEO (search engine optimization):** the win is a ranked position that earns a click.
- **AEO (answer engine optimization):** earning a place in the answer itself. The label covers answer boxes such as [featured snippets](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/featured-snippets) and increasingly AI answers ([AEO explainer](/blog/what-is-answer-engine-optimization)).
- **GEO (generative engine optimization):** a term from a [2023 research paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735) (Aggarwal et al., KDD 2024) on visibility in engines that retrieve sources and write a response ([GEO guide](/blog/generative-engine-optimization)).

sections.heading: How do SEO, AEO and GEO compare side by side?
sections.body:
They differ on what counts as a win: SEO wins a ranked position; AEO and GEO win a mention inside the answer.

| | SEO | AEO | GEO |
|---|---|---|---|
| Goal | Rank a page so people click | Be the answer an engine shows | Be named in an AI-written answer |
| Shows up in | Search results pages | Featured snippets, AI answers | ChatGPT search, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode |
| Unit of success | A ranked position, then a click | A place in the answer | A mention or citation |
| Main metrics | Impressions, clicks, CTR, position | Snippets held, answers that name you | Share of answers that name or cite you |
| Core tactics | Crawlable, useful, linked pages matching intent | Direct, self-contained answers on indexed pages | Evidence-backed passages, accurate facts, third-party mentions |
| Time to impact | Hours to several months | Same clock as SEO for snippets | Next crawl for live-search answers; new models for memory |

In the last row, the SEO range is [Google's](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/seo-starter-guide); the AI cells are our reading. Why the unit of success matters:

- In [Pew Research's March 2025 browsing data](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/), US users clicked a traditional result in 8% of visits with a Google AI summary and 15% without, and a link inside the summary in 1%.
- In [AEOeye's recommendation benchmark](/resources/aeoeye-recommendation-benchmark-2026-09.json) (127 audits, 892 answers, small and self-selected), when an answer ranked the audited brand (147 cases), it came first 71.4% of the time.

sections.heading: Are AEO and GEO actually different?
sections.body:
Not in any way that changes your work. Both labels aim at the same outcome, being named in an engine's answer, and Google's guide treats them as names for one kind of work. Only two things differ:

- **Origin:** GEO has a founding paper; AEO has no comparable one that we found.
- **Emphasis:** AEO also covers answer boxes such as featured snippets; GEO targets AI-written answers.

What the research adds: in the GEO paper's 10,000-query benchmark, adding citations, quotations or statistics lifted a source's visibility roughly 30 to 40% on its word-count metric, while keyword stuffing did little. Those were 2023-era tests on a research-built engine and Perplexity, so read them as direction, not forecast. Google says its AI features need [no special files, markup, schema, chunking or AI-specific rewriting](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide), and warns that seeking inauthentic mentions is less useful than it looks.

Our position: treat AEO and GEO as one discipline, use the label your audience searches for, and don't pay extra for it. If an agency prices them separately, ask which task differs. We merged our own AEO-versus-GEO posts into this page in October 2026 for the same reason. For what is genuinely new, read [Most AEO advice is recycled SEO](/blog/most-aeo-advice-is-recycled-seo).

sections.heading: What do SEO, AEO and GEO have in common?
sections.body:
All three depend on the same gate and the same raw material. The gate is access: a crawler can fetch your page and the engine can index it. The raw material is content: [Google says](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) unique, useful content will likely do more for its AI features than any other suggestion in its guide.

On access, Google says a page must be [indexed and eligible to show with a snippet](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) to appear as a supporting link in Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode. OpenAI says sites that opt out of OAI-SearchBot [are not shown in ChatGPT search answers](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots).

In AEOeye's crawler access study (3 October 2026; 384 sites, a convenience sample), Googlebot and Bingbot were disallowed on one site, Reddit. By contrast, 37 sites (9.6%) disallowed at least one AI retrieval bot, including 27 of 38 news publishers but 1 of 193 SaaS sites. The [summary and method](/resources/ai-crawler-access-study-2026-10.json) and [per-site CSV](/resources/ai-crawler-access-study-2026-10.csv) are public (one fetch per site, one day). For brands, access is rarely the problem; two quieter failures are:

- **Blocking the wrong crawler.** OpenAI says its crawler settings are independent: blocking GPTBot (training) does not remove you from ChatGPT search, and 19 of 384 sites (4.9%) run exactly that split.
- **Bot protection.** 24 of 88 e-commerce and consumer homepages (27.3%) challenged or blocked our self-identified crawler. That does not prove they block AI bots, but OpenAI recommends allowing its published IP ranges, so check your CDN logs.

sections.heading: Which one does your business need?
sections.body:
Start with SEO, then test whether AI answers name you. If answers to your buyers' questions name competitors and skip you, add AEO and GEO work, most urgently where buyers ask for shortlists. If answers name you, or name no brands in your category, SEO alone is enough for now. The test takes an afternoon:

1. Write 10 unbranded questions a buyer asks before choosing, such as "best CRM for agencies".
2. Ask each in ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini, rephrased and repeated.
3. Record whether you are named, in what position, and who appears instead.

Then read the result by symptom:

- **You rank well, but AI names rivals:** an AEO and GEO problem. [Research on AI search](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08919) found these engines lean on third-party sources far more than Google does, so get described accurately on other sites and put evidence in your own pages.
- **AI cannot describe you even when asked by name:** a crawl, entity or trust problem, so SEO first. Check robots.txt, CDN logs and indexing.
- **Google's AI names you but ChatGPT does not:** a source-mix problem. The same research found AI search services differ in domain diversity and freshness, so check which sources each one cites.
- **Named everywhere, revenue flat:** not a visibility problem. Check how answers describe you and what happens after the click.

sections.heading: How do you measure each without fooling yourself?
sections.body:
Use a different instrument for each layer, and never use rank as a stand-in for being named.

- **Google:** the [Performance report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7576553) in Search Console shows clicks, impressions, CTR and position, and [includes AI-feature traffic](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) in its Web search type. The [generative AI performance report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16984139) adds impressions in Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode (available to all websites as of October 2026, with conditions).
- **Microsoft Copilot:** [AI Performance in Bing Webmaster Tools](https://blogs.bing.com/webmaster/February-2026/Introducing-AI-Performance-in-Bing-Webmaster-Tools-Public-Preview) launched in public preview in February 2026. It counts citations, and Microsoft says it does not indicate ranking.
- **ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini:** we know of no comparable first-party report, so you sample answers.

Sampling fails in two ways:

- **One answer is not a measurement.** A July 2026 [preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13304) on 12,933 AI responses about 20 brands found brand-ranking reliability near 0.01 for a single answer, and spreading questions across models and languages helped more than repeating one prompt.
- **Unequal samples mislead.** Claude supplied 509 of the benchmark's 892 answers and four engines had fewer than 10 mentions, so we do not rank engines. Our [measurement guide](/blog/ai-brand-recommendation-measurement) shows a fair setup.

For a first pass, [AEOeye's free audit](/) asks three unbranded buyer questions to ChatGPT and shows the answers in full; for daily tracking across hundreds of prompts, dedicated trackers such as Profound, Peec AI or Otterly fit better.

![Detailed view of a classic mechanical balance scale](https://images.pexels.com/photos/16204377/pexels-photo-16204377.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

keyTakeaways: SEO wins a ranked click; AEO and GEO win a mention in the answer, two labels for one discipline.
All three need crawl and index access first.
Run a ten-question test; if AI answers name your rivals and skip you, add AEO and GEO work.
Measure by repeating a fixed question set across engines; one answer proves nothing.

faqs.q: Is AEO the same as GEO?
faqs.a: In practice, yes. Both aim to get your brand named inside an AI-written answer, and Google's guide lists them together as terms for AI search visibility work. GEO has a founding paper (Aggarwal et al., 2023); AEO is the looser label, also used for featured snippets. Use whichever your audience already searches for.

faqs.q: Which term should I use: AEO, GEO or AI SEO?
faqs.a: Use the one your audience already understands and define it once on the page. The label matters less than the scoreboard: are you named in answers to your buyers' questions? Google lists AEO and GEO together as terms for AI search visibility work, so judge any vendor by what it measures and fixes, not by which acronym it sells.

faqs.q: Do I still need SEO if I focus on AEO or GEO?
faqs.a: Yes. Google says a page must be indexed and eligible to show with a snippet to appear as a supporting link in Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode, and OpenAI says sites that opt out of OAI-SearchBot are not shown in ChatGPT search answers. SEO is the gate; AEO and GEO work decides whether you are named once you are through it.

faqs.q: Where does the term GEO come from?
faqs.a: From a paper titled GEO: Generative Engine Optimization by Aggarwal et al., posted to arXiv in November 2023 and presented at KDD 2024. It introduced a 10,000-query benchmark and reported visibility gains of up to 40%. The tests used a research-built engine and Perplexity, so they show a direction, not a guarantee for ChatGPT or Google.

faqs.q: What should I measure instead of keyword rankings?
faqs.a: Measure whether you are named. Take ten questions your buyers ask, run them on each engine several times with varied wording, and record how often you appear and who appears instead. Keep rankings and clicks for SEO. Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools now report impressions and citations on Google's and Microsoft's own AI surfaces.

definitions.definition: A box in Google results that reverses the usual layout and shows a descriptive snippet first. Google's systems choose the page automatically; site owners cannot request one, only opt out of snippets.

A search system that retrieves relevant documents and uses a large language model to write a response grounded in those sources, with attribution. The GEO paper formalizes the idea and names the practice of optimizing visibility in their responses.
OpenAI's two main crawlers, controlled separately in robots.txt. GPTBot collects content to improve OpenAI's generative AI foundation models; OAI-SearchBot surfaces sites in ChatGPT search.
